title-group.article-title: Mathematical Modelling of the Three-Dimensional Free Vibration of Bidirectionally Graded Porous Plates on a Kerr Foundation: A Rayleigh–Ritz Eigenvalue Approach

contrib-group.aff: Department of Mathematics, College of Science, Taif University, 21944 Taif, Saudi Arabia

license.license-p: Published by Acadlore Publishing Services Limited, Hong Kong. This article is available for free download and can be reused and cited, provided that the original published version is credited, under the CC BY 4.0 license.

abstract.p: This paper develops a mathematical model for the three-dimensional (3D) free vibration of porous plates whose material properties are graded along the length and through the thickness and which rest on a three-parameter Kerr foundation. The problem is formulated as an eigenvalue problem for the 3D elasticity operator with coefficients that vary in two coordinates, and it is solved by the Rayleigh–Ritz method. The trial functions are numerically orthonormalised Legendre polynomials, the separable structure of the coefficients turns every matrix block into a Kronecker product, and the massless foundation field is eliminated by static condensation, which leads to a symmetric generalized matrix eigenvalue problem. The model is verified against an independent exact solution, obtained for thickness-dependent coefficients from a two-point boundary-value problem for six first-order differential equations, and against classical results for homogeneous plates; its convergence is examined for different edge conditions. Two reduced two-dimensional models, a higher-order shear deformation theory and a reduced-unknown quasi-3D theory, are formulated in the same framework and assessed against the 3D model. The results show that in-plane grading lowers the eigenvalues considerably and makes the eigenfunctions asymmetric, that a stiff foundation can turn an in-plane mode into the fundamental mode, and that porosity lowers the frequency of an unsupported plate but raises it on a stiff foundation. The higher-order theory agrees closely with the 3D model for simply supported plates of moderate and small thickness, whereas the quasi-3D theory retains a noticeable error even for very thin thickness-graded plates because of thickness locking. New 3D benchmark eigenvalues are provided.

sec.title: 1. Introduction
sec.p: Many problems of applied mechanics lead to eigenvalue problems for partial differential operators with variable coefficients. The free vibration of a plate whose material properties change from point to point is a typical example: the natural frequencies and mode shapes are the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the three-dimensional (3D) elasticity operator, whose coefficients follow the spatial distribution of the stiffness and the density. Closed-form solutions exist only when the coefficients depend on a single coordinate and the boundary conditions allow a separation of variables. In all other cases the problem must be approximated, and two questions then arise: how to construct a discretisation that is accurate, well conditioned and verifiable, and how much accuracy is lost when the 3D problem is replaced by a simpler two-dimensional (2D) model.

Functionally graded materials (FGMs) give rise to exactly such problems. Their composition changes continuously, typically from a ceramic on one face to a metal on the other [1]. When the service conditions also vary along a component, the composition can be graded in a second direction, which gives more freedom to tailor the stiffness and the thermal stresses than one-directional grading [2], [3]. The static and dynamic behaviour of these bidirectional FGMs has been studied for beams [4], [5] and plates [6], [7], [8], [9], [10], [11]. Mathematically, grading along the length as well as through the thickness makes the coefficients of the governing equations depend on two coordinates. The Fourier-series solutions available for thickness-graded plates then no longer apply, even for simply supported edges.

For plates graded through the thickness only, the free-vibration problem is well understood. Vel and Batra [12] obtained exact 3D solutions for simply supported plates, Uymaz and Aydogdu [13] used a 3D Ritz method for other edge conditions, and Matsunaga [14] and Hosseini-Hashemi et al. [15] gave higher-order and first-order plate solutions. The Rayleigh–Ritz method with polynomial trial functions is particularly suited to such problems [13], [16], [17]: it handles arbitrary combinations of edge conditions, it converges from above to the exact eigenvalues, and the trial functions need to satisfy only the essential boundary conditions. Its main numerical difficulty is the ill-conditioning of the mass and stiffness matrices when high-degree polynomials are used, which limits the attainable accuracy. Reduced 2D models are an alternative. Shear deformation theories and quasi-3D theories, which add a transverse normal strain, have been proposed with full expansions [18], [19] and with a reduced number of unknowns [20], [21], [22], [23], [24]. They replace the 3D eigenvalue problem by a smaller one, but their accuracy has to be established against 3D solutions. Plates on two- and three-parameter elastic foundations have been analysed with such models [25], [26], [27], and Zhou et al. [16] gave 3D Ritz solutions for thick homogeneous plates on a Pasternak foundation.

For bidirectionally graded plates the available results are based on reduced models only. Melaibari et al. [7] studied the free vibration of bidirectional graded porous plates on elastic foundations with a 2D differential quadrature method, and Lieu et al. [11] analysed the bending and free vibration of in-plane bidirectional plates by isogeometric analysis. Kerr-foundation studies have addressed the thermal vibration of bidirectionally stepped porous plates [28] and the free vibration of thickness-graded porous plates with a quasi-3D theory [29]. To the author’s knowledge, no 3D solutions are available for the free vibration of plates graded along the length and through the thickness on a Kerr foundation. Without them the accuracy of the reduced models cannot be assessed. This matters because, for the same plates under mechanical load, the reduced-unknown quasi-3D theory was found to be slightly stiffer than the 3D solution because of thickness locking, and in-plane grading shifted the peak deflection away from the plate centre [30]. Both effects can be expected to influence the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions as well.
This paper develops and verifies a mathematical model for this eigenvalue problem. The main contributions are as follows:

p.p: A 3D Rayleigh–Ritz formulation is constructed for a plate whose stiffness and density vary in two coordinates and which rests on a three-parameter Kerr foundation. The trial functions are Legendre polynomials with boundary factors, orthonormalised numerically to keep the matrices well conditioned. The separable structure of the coefficients is exploited so that every matrix block becomes a Kronecker product. The massless foundation field is eliminated by static condensation, which leads to a symmetric generalized eigenvalue problem for the plate alone.

An independent exact solution is derived for the case in which the coefficients depend on the thickness coordinate only. The problem is reduced to a two-point boundary-value problem for a system of six first-order ordinary differential equations, and the eigenvalues are obtained as roots of a boundary determinant. This solution, together with classical results for homogeneous plates, verifies the Ritz model, and its convergence is examined for different edge conditions.

Two reduced 2D models, a higher-order shear deformation theory (HSDT) and a reduced-unknown quasi-3D theory, are formulated within the same Rayleigh–Ritz framework and assessed against the 3D model over a range of thickness ratios, gradation indices and edge conditions.

New 3D benchmark eigenvalues are provided, and a parametric study shows how the gradation indices, porosity, the three foundation parameters, the edge conditions and the thickness ratio affect the eigenvalues and the shape of the eigenfunctions. A kinetic-energy criterion is introduced to distinguish flexural from in-plane modes.

sec.p: The paper is organised as follows. Section 2 presents the mathematical model, Section 3 the Rayleigh–Ritz discretisation, Section 4 the verification, the assessment of the reduced models and the parametric study, and Section 5 the conclusions.

sec.p: Table 6 and Table 7 give new 3D results for future comparison: the first six frequencies, with in-plane modes marked, for plates on the reference Kerr foundation (SSSS, CSCS and CCCC edges) and for SSSS plates without a foundation. sec.title: 5. Conclusions
sec.p: The free vibration of length- and thickness-graded porous plates resting on a three-parameter Kerr foundation was studied with a 3D elasticity Ritz model and two plate theories. The main conclusions are:

p.p: A 3D Ritz model with a statically condensed Kerr foundation reproduces an independent exact state-space solution to all reported digits and the classical results of Srinivas et al. for homogeneous plates. New 3D benchmark frequencies are provided for bidirectional porous plates with and without a Kerr foundation (Table 6 and Table 7).

In-plane grading lowers the natural frequencies, because aluminium has a much lower stiffness-to-density ratio than alumina. From \(k_x=0\) to \(k_x=5\) the fundamental frequency falls by about one third without a foundation, and moderately on the reference Kerr foundation.

In-plane grading makes the mode shapes asymmetric. The peak of the first mode moves toward the metal-rich edge (to \(x/a\approx 0.41\)–\(0.46\) for \(k_x\approx 2\)), degenerate mode pairs of square plates split, and nodal lines move toward the ceramic-rich edge. A stiff foundation moves the peak back across the centre toward the heavier, ceramic-rich edge.

The HSDT agrees closely with the 3D solution for SSSS plates with \(a/h\geq 10\), and its error vanishes for thin plates. The reduced-unknown quasi-3D theory is not more accurate. For thickness-graded plates it retains a noticeable error even for \(a/h=50\), a consequence of thickness locking. This error decreases with in-plane grading.

The Kerr upper spring acts in series with the shear layer and the lower spring. Stiff foundations raise only the flexural frequencies, so the first in-plane mode, which is coupled to bending in bidirectional plates, can become the fundamental mode of the plate.

The effect of porosity depends on the foundation. It lowers the frequency of an unsupported plate, considerably so for strongly graded bidirectional plates, has little effect on the reference foundation and raises the flexural frequency on a stiff foundation.
In bidirectional plates, clamping the graded edges and clamping the ungraded edges give different frequencies and mode shapes, while the two cases coincide for thickness-graded plates.

sec.p: For sensitive structural designs involving thick plates, clamped edges or stiff foundations, simplified 2D and reduced-unknown quasi-3D models should be checked against exact 3D elasticity or benchmarked Ritz solutions, since thickness locking and the coupling of bending and stretching can affect the predicted frequencies and modes.

Further work can address forced and transient vibration, thermal pre-stress, and the vibration of plates on tensionless foundations, for which the contact region must be determined as part of the solution.
